about: Plain-language definitions of the things the revival assumes you already know.

terms.definition: The fictional historically Black college the whole franchise is set in — in Virginia, introduced on The Cosby Show before being given its own series in 1987. Its dormitories, radio station, pageant and money problems are the original's furniture, and the revival keeps all of it.
The dormitory the original's first season is set in — named for Whitley Gilbert's family. In 2026 Whitley and Dwayne's daughter moves into it, and Hazel competes for Miss Gilbert Hall inside it.

The campus pageant. Whitley entered the original's Miss Hillman pageant in 1988 chasing her mother's approval; Hazel runs for Miss Gilbert Hall in 2026. It is the show's standing argument about class, colour and who gets crowned.
The campus food spot, run by Mr. Gaines, where students worked — Whitley took a job there to pay off a car she damaged. When a character needs money in this franchise, the Pit is usually the answer.

A Black fraternity and sorority performance tradition, performed in formation with rhythmic footwork. The original staged it as a homecoming competition (Whitley choreographing Gilbert Hall's routine) and as a unity ritual, and the revival keeps it as campus ritual.

Historically Black colleges and universities — US institutions founded before the Civil Rights Act of 1964 with the intention of serving African American students, most of them in the South and mostly founded during Reconstruction. Hillman is fictional; the funding, tuition dependence and load-bearing role in Black mobility are not.

The nickname students gave Col. Bradford Taylor, the professor whose calculus class Dwayne tried to dodge and then credited with changing him. Glynn Turman recurs as him in 2026 — the name is an 1988 joke the audience is expected to remember.

The revival's shorthand for the returning original characters — Jaleesa, Kimberly, Davenport, Gina, Charmaine, Darlene, Lena. The 2026 joke is literal: the people who were the students are now the women who arrive at the club.

Lisa Bonet's character — a Cosby Show daughter who became the spin-off's first lead, moved into Gilbert Hall in 1987, and left during the first season, after which the show re-centred on Whitley and Dwayne. The revival's lead is the daughter of the couple who replaced her.

Whitley's recurring unseen ideal man in the original — invoked to describe the imaginary perfect partner. Deborah's 2026 version of the same problem is the 'ideal partner' episode. (Listed because fan glossaries always have it; not used on this page as a citation.)

A Different World began as a Cosby Show spin-off in 1987; the 2026 revival is a sequel to that series. Deborah Wayne is therefore a third-generation television character — she exists because a family on a 1984 sitcom had a daughter who went to college.
